subject: Scope definition: suppressing sensitive headers in logs (request/response)
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@brightwell.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-02T15:08:00-08:00
Subject: Scope definition: suppressing sensitive headers in logs (request/response)

Hi Elliot —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed minimal scope so everyone is aligned before Ben and Rishi jump in with technical options.

Summary of ask from Brightwell: you want Redwood to avoid persisting or to proactively redact sensitive request/response items from our standard logging pipeline for the integration that will touch payment-card verification flows. The priority controls you mentioned were:
- Never store full request/response bodies with card numbers or PII
- Strip or obfuscate identifying headers (Cookie, Authorization, Trace-ID variants) before any long-term log retention
- Ability to set per-environment retention windows (e.g., dev: 7 days, prod: 30 days) and to support EU residency for customer logs

Proposed minimal scope for initial PO/POC:
1) Implement request/response suppression rule that drops full bodies for endpoints matching /payment/* and replaces bodies with a redaction stub ("[REDACTED_BODY]").
2) Header suppression policy: configuration-driven list to remove or hash headers before writing to logs (default set: Authorization, Cookie, X-Forwarded-For, X-Trace-Id, Traceparent).
3) Configurable retention/region knob per-customer so Brightwell can pin logs generated to an EU region when required.
4) Provide a short evidence bundle for your security team: config snapshot + sample sanitized logs and a short writeup of guarantees.

Next steps (recommended):
- Ben to propose two implementation approaches and trade-offs (fast path: runtime suppression hooks; longer-term: streaming pipeline sanitizer with schema enforcement).
- Brightwell to share their initial list of endpoints and a short CSV of sample payloads (anonymous where possible).
- Rishi to confirm compliance packaging needs (SOC2 artifact checklist, retention proof).

I've attached the short survey you filled out (brightwell_survey.csv) and a template for requirements that you can add to (redaction_requirements.pdf).

If that matches your expectation I can turn this into an internal MR and estimate a POC timeline (2–3 sprints for a minimal runtime hook + config).

Best,
Priya
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0172

From: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@brightwell.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightwell Analytics - Security Team <security@brightwell.ai>
Date: 2027-12-02T18:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scope definition: suppressing sensitive headers in logs (request/response)

Thanks Priya — this is very close to what we discussed. A few clarifications and a question from security: 

1) For "replace bodies with a redaction stub" — can Redwood provide a tamper-proof hash of the original body (one-way) in the sanitized log so we can correlate retried requests without storing the raw payload? If hashing is optional we need to understand algorithm and salt handling.
2) Trace IDs: we use an internal trace-id (X-BW-Trace) plus vendor-generated trace headers; security wants the ability to redact or consistently replace trace values across systems so we can still link events but not expose identifiers in long-term logs.
3) Evidence bundle: security asked for a brief tech note describing the suppression point (runtime vs pipeline) and a sample sanitized log event for both a dev and prod retention policy.

I'll attach a short doc with our priority endpoints and a sample payloads list (sensitive fields blanked). Also note: we have a contractual requirement to keep diagnostic logs for only 30 days in prod unless otherwise approved.

If you can confirm the hash approach and whether Redwood can pin log residency to the eu-west-1 region for our prod project, we can move to a POC statement of work.

Elliot
Elliot Shaw
Head of Security Engineering, Brightwell Analytics
elliot.shaw@brightwell.ai
+1 617-555-1209

Attachments: redaction_requirements.pdf (uploaded by Brightwell; has comments)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@brightwell.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-03T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scope definition: suppressing sensitive headers in logs (request/response)

Elliot — thanks, clear asks. Quick technical response and recommended options so you can pick a POC path: 

Option A (fast, low effort) — Runtime suppression hooks:
- At the serving runtime, add a configurable suppression policy evaluated per-request. If endpoint matches, runtime will:
  * drop full request/response bodies from structured logs and emit a stub body with metadata (status, size, truncated flag)
  * replace each header in the suppression list with a one-way SHA-256 hex hash (we can include a 16-byte prefix of the hash to keep logs compact)
  * for trace IDs we can either: (1) replace with a stable pseudonym per-tenant (HMAC with tenant key) so you can correlate; or (2) redact completely.
- Pros: fastest (days), minimal infra changes. Cons: no central reprocessing if you need to recover originals.

Option B (recommended for longer term) — Streaming sanitizer pipeline:
- Stream logs through a sanitizer layer before long-term storage; sanitizer enforces schemas, strips fields, and writes to region-specific buckets.
- Hashing/pseudonymization keys managed in KMS; per-tenant key rotation supported.
- Pros: auditable, reprocess capability, easier to support retention windows by lifecycle policies. Cons: more infra (weeks to ship), larger initial cost.

On the hash question: we can produce a one-way HMAC-SHA256 per-tenant (using a tenant-specific key stored in KMS). That satisfies not storing raw payloads while allowing you to correlate across retries and services if you keep the same tenant key. We will document the key lifecycle and provide an artifact showing the HMAC process for SOC2 reviewers.

Region pinning: we support prefixing logs to region-specific buckets. For the POC we can pin prod logs for Brightwell to eu-west-1; we'll include a configuration toggle in the POC MR.

Next steps I propose:
- Brightwell: provide sample endpoints CSV and confirm desire for HMAC pseudonymization vs full redact for trace IDs.
- Priya: I will draft an SOW for the POC (runtime suppression hook + evidence bundle) estimating 3 weeks dev + 1 week QA.
- Rishi: please add any compliance items we should include in the evidence pack.

I'll attach an examples-config.txt with config snippets for both options.

—Ben

Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
